references.text: Here the actual collection of the atonement money is described and how the silver was used for the service of the tabernacle, as a fulfillment of the command in Exod 30:16.
The officers brought gold as an offering to the Lord to make atonement for their souls, similar to the concept of atonement money as a reminder before the Lord.
The bronze plates became a memorial (זִכָּרוֹן) for the children of Israel, using the same word that is used for the atonement money as a reminder before the Lord.
Passover was to be a day of remembrance (זִכָּרוֹן) for Israel, the same concept as the atonement money serving as a reminder before the Lord.
Explains the principle of atonement (כַּפֵּר) for the soul, which is the theological basis for the atonement money.
Jesus gave his life as a ransom (λύτρον) for many, fulfilling and surpassing the function of the atonement money in the OT.
Believers were redeemed not with perishable things like silver or gold, but with the precious blood of Christ—a contrast to the atonement money made of silver.
The means of atonement from Exod 30:16 are applied concretely in the ritual for cleansing the sanctuary because of the people's sins in Lev 16:16.
Exod 30:16 establishes the means (money) for atonement, while Lev 16:34 sets that this must happen as a permanent statute once a year.
Lev 16:33 clarifies what the atonement money from Exod 30:16 is to cover: atonement for the sanctuary, the tent, and all the people.
Both verses link atonement to preventing the children of Israel from being struck by plague due to their proximity to the sanctuary.
